\n\n[Getafe](/football/getafe/) \n\n# Preview: Athletic Bilbao vs Getafe - prediction, team news, lineups\n\nBy [Matt Law](/team/matt-law/) | 23 Oct 2026 13:17, Last updated: 23 Oct 2026 13:20 \n\n![Athletic Bilbao vs Getafe - prediction, team news, lineups](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/thumbor/x24GkMgRyIPKE4Rb4wV4qNqAjFs=/720x540/smart/filters:format\\(webp\\)/https%3A%2F%2Fsportsmole-media-prod.s3.gra.io.cloud.ovh.net%2Fuploads%2F2026%2F08%2Fimago1082070706-1-6a91b63637729075031318.jpg) \n\n© Imago / NurPhoto\n\nBoth [Athletic Bilbao](/football/athletic-bilbao/ \"Athletic Bilbao\") and [Getafe](/football/getafe/ \"Getafe\") will be aiming to return to winning ways in Spain's top flight when they lock horns at San Mames on Sunday afternoon.\n\nAthletic were beaten 3-1 by Levante in La Liga last time out, while Getafe drew 1-1 with Rayo Vallecano in their last domestic fixture.\n\n* * *\n\n## Match preview\n\nAthletic have had an underwhelming start to the campaign, boasting a record of two wins, three draws and three defeats from eight matches, with nine points leaving them 13th in the **[La Liga table](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/la-liga/table.html)**.\n\nThe Lions have not been victorious in Spain's top flight since a 3-0 home success over Atletico Madrid at the start of September, collecting just three points from their last four matches.\n\n[Edin Terzic](/people/edin-terzic/ \"Edin Terzic\")'s side drew three straight games against Elche, Alaves and Valencia before having a player sent off in a 3-1 defeat to Levante on October 21.\n\nAthletic finished 12th in Spain's top flight last season, so there is plenty of room for improvement during the current campaign.\n\nThe Lions lost both league games against Getafe during the 2025-26 campaign, including a 1-0 reverse at San Mames last October.\n\n![](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/thumbor/8u0HppeMFS7t_6fx0Pyq_nK6qh0=/640x480/smart/filters:format\\(webp\\)/https%3A%2F%2Fsportsmole-media-prod.s3.gra.io.cloud.ovh.net%2Fuploads%2F2026%2F08%2Fgetafe-4-6a84e59ad3680561087588.jpg)\n\n© Imago / Ricardo Larreina Amador\n\nGetafe have only lost two of their last 10 matches against Athletic, although six of those fixtures have finished all square, pointing to a close game this weekend.\n\n[Jose Bordalas](/people/jose-bordalas/ \"Jose Bordalas\")' side were in European action on Thursday evening, suffering a 5-2 home defeat to Lugano, leaving them with one point from two Conference League fixtures.\n\nGetafe drew 1-1 with Rayo in La Liga last time out, and they currently sit 15th in the table, with two wins, three draws and four defeats from nine matches giving them nine points.\n\nThe Deep Blue Ones finished seventh in Spain's top flight last season, but they have struggled for consistency in the early stages of this campaign.\n\nAthletic Bilbao La Liga News\n\n![](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/thumbor/1EMGktPnNBP88iOhUEiKcNQ2cm4=/640x480/smart/filters:format\\(webp\\)/https%3A%2F%2Fsportsmole-media-prod.s3.gra.io.cloud.ovh.net%2F25%2F02%2Finaki-williams.jpg)\n\n© Imago\n\nAthletic will be without the services of Aymeric Laporte through suspension, with the experienced defender sent off in the defeat to Levante last time out.\n\nMeanwhile, Gorka Guruzeta, Oihan Sancet and Unai Egiluz are again expected to be absent through injury; Alvaro Djalo also needs to be assessed due to a recent illness.\n\n[Nico Williams](/people/nico-williams/ \"Nico Williams\") and Inaki Williams both came off the bench against Levante, and the pair are now expected to be brought back into the starting side.\n\nAs for Getafe, Djene Dakonam will miss out through suspension, having been sent off in the team's draw with Rayo Vallecano last time out.\n\nThere will be changes to the side that took to the field against Lugano in the Conference League, with Martin Satriano, Enes Unal, Ramon Terrats and Nemanja Gudelj expected to be among those introduced back into the starting side.\n\nMeanwhile, there will be another start at right-back for the experienced Dani Carvajal.\n\n**Athletic Bilbao possible starting lineup:**\n\nSimon; Rincon, Alvarez, Paredes, Berchiche; Ruiz de Galarreta, Jauregizar; Berenguer, Navarro, N Williams; I Williams\n\n**Getafe possible vs Getafe Preview: Team News & Prediction\n\nby [Alex Lawes](https://www.thestatszone.com/author/alexl) · 23 October 2026 at 10:38 am \n\n ![Athletic Bilbao vs Getafe Preview: Team News & Prediction](https://www.thestatszone.com/imager/211241/1785278238_b0464c6958.jpg)\n\n[Post](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?&text=Athletic%20Bilbao%20vs%20Getafe%20Preview%3A%20Team%20News%20%26%20Prediction%0A%0Ahttps://www.thestatszone.com/athletic-bilbao-vs-getafe-preview-team-news-prediction-232335) [Share](https://facebook.com/share.php?u=https://www.thestatszone.com/athletic-bilbao-vs-getafe-preview-team-news-prediction-232335) \n\n[**Click here for today’s sports betting tips from our expert analysts!**](https://www.thestatszone.com/betting-tips)\n\n*Athletic Club now find themselves under a bit of pressure as the Basque giants now welcome a very busy Getafe side to San Mames on Sunday.*\n\n**Kick-off date/time:** 25 October 2026 at 1:00 pm \n\n**How to watch on TV:** UK – Premier Sports / USA – ESPN have the exclusive rights to La Liga games in the USA, so any game may be televised on one of their affiliated channels\n\n**How to watch online:** UK – Premier Player / USA – ESPN+\n\n**Athletic Bilbao preview: Tough start**\n\nThere were signs of life for Athletic after back-to-back victories against Celta Vigo and Atletico Madrid in early-September but former Borussia Dortmund boss Edin Terzic is finding it difficult to bring about some consistency in Bilbao.\n\nThey now head into this one on the back of a comfortable 3-1 defeat at the hands of Levante at Estadio Ciutat de Valencia in midweek due to an early brace from Brugui, a consolation from Alex Berenguer and then a late consolation scored by Karl Etta Eyong.\n\n**Getafe preview: Busy Getafe**\n\nGetafe come into this one on the back of a 5-2 hammering at the hands of Swiss Super League outfit Lugano in the league phase of the UEFA Europa Conference League in midweek in a game in which they were simply blown away at the Coliseum.\n\nIn La Liga, Getafe have managed just three victories in their 13 matches across all competitions so far this season as they look set to battle against the drop with an underwhelming style of football as ever under Jose Bordalas.\n\n**Athletic Bilbao team news: Laporte suspended**\n\nFIFA World Cup 2026 winning defender Aymeric Laporte was sent off last week and so is now missing through suspension with Oihan Sancet also still unavailable but Nico Williams has returned to full fitness for the hosts.\n\n**Predicted XI (4-2-3-1):** Unai Simon; Hugo Rincon, Yeray, Aitor Paredes, Yuri Berchiche; Inigo Ruiz de Galarreta, Benat Gerenabarrena; Robert Navarro, Alex Berenguer, Nico Williams; Inaki Williams\n\n**Unavailable:** Laporte (Suspended), Unai Egiluz (Injured), Oihan Sancet (Injured), Gorka Guruzeta (Injured)\n\n**Questionable:** Alvaro Djalo (Injured)\n\n**Getafe team news: Unal a doubt**\n\nEnes Unal was forced off with an ankle injury against Lugano in midweek with versatile defender Djene now missing through suspension after being sent off last weekend.\n\n**Predicted XI (4-4-2):** David Soria; Dani Carvajal, Abqar, Valou, Johan Mojica; Kiko Femenia, Gudelj, Mario Martin, Ramon Terrats; Martin Satriano, Ivan Azon\n\n**Unavailable:** Djene (Suspended), Uche (Injured), Juanmi (Injured)\n\n**Questionable:** Romero (Fitness), Mangala (Fitness), Unal (Injured)\n\n**Key stats**\n\n*   Eighteen of the 42 La Liga meetings since 1997/98 have been draws (43%): Athletic W13 D18 Getafe W11. \n*   Athletic are winless in the last five home meetings (D4 L1). Their last home win against Getafe was 5-1 in January 2021, the highest-scoring game in the fixture. \n*   Getafe won both meetings last season without conceding, including 1-0 at San Mamés exactly a year ago (25 October 2025). Athletic have failed to score in the last two meetings. \n*   Athletic have played only seven games – two fewer than 17 of the other 19 sides – and have nine points. They are unbeaten in five (W2 D3). \n*   Athletic have drawn their last three and have kept two straight clean sheets in 0-0 draws with Alavés and Valencia. \n*   Athletic's matches have averaged 1.86 goals this season, down from 2.66 last season. \n*   Getafe have not scored an away goal this season: four away games, four defeats, 0-8 on aggregate. \n*   Getafe have lost five consecutive La Liga away games and failed to score in six, dating back to May 2026. \n*   Getafe are unbeaten in seven home games, scoring in all seven. \n*   Getafe have scored only five goals – only one of their previous 21 La Liga seasons since 1997/98 had as few or fewer after nine games. \n*   Getafe's matches have averaged 1.78 goals this season. \n\n*Statistics are La Liga only (not all competitions)*\n\n**Athletic Bilbao vs Getafe prediction**\n\nIn nine matches in La Liga, the often tedious style of Jose Bordalas has seen Getafe score just five goals as they remain the lowest scorers in Spain’s top-flight. Athletic themselves have lacked fluency in the final third despite the intentions of manager Terzic and they will nervy about a Getafe side that may become ultra-Getafe after their hammering the other day and so a low-scoring contest feels likely for this one.\n\n**Athletic Bilbao vs Getafe tip:** Under 2.5 goals\n\nUpcoming Sunday.*\n\n**Kick-off date/time:** 25 October 2026 at 1:00 pm \n\n**How to watch on TV:** UK – Premier Sports / USA – ESPN have the exclusive rights to La Liga games in the USA, so any game may be televised on one of their affiliated channels\n\n**How to watch online:** UK – Premier Player / USA – ESPN+\n\n**Athletic Bilbao preview: Tough start**\n\nThere were signs of life for Athletic after back-to-back victories against Celta Vigo and Atletico Madrid in early-September but former Borussia Dortmund boss Edin Terzic is finding it difficult to bring about some consistency in Bilbao.\n\nThey now head into this one on the back of a comfortable 3-1 defeat at the hands of Levante at Estadio Ciutat de Valencia in midweek due to an early brace from Brugui, a consolation from Alex Berenguer and then a late consolation scored by Karl Etta Eyong.\n\n**Getafe preview: Busy Getafe**\n\nGetafe come into this one on the back of a 5-2 hammering at the hands of Swiss Super League outfit Lugano in the league phase of the UEFA Europa Conference League in midweek in a game in which they were simply blown away at the Coliseum.\n\nIn La Liga, Getafe have managed just three victories in their 13 matches across all competitions so far this season as they look set to battle against the drop with an underwhelming style of football as ever under Jose Bordalas.\n\n**Athletic Bilbao team news: Laporte suspended**\n\nFIFA World Cup 2026 winning defender Aymeric Laporte was sent off last week and so is now missing through suspension with Oihan Sancet also still unavailable but Nico Williams has returned to full fitness for the hosts.\n\n**Predicted XI (4-2-3-1):** Unai Simon; Hugo Rincon, Yeray, Aitor Paredes, Yuri Berchiche; Inigo Ruiz de Galarreta, Benat Gerenabarrena; Robert Navarro, Alex Berenguer, Nico Williams; Inaki Williams\n\n**Unavailable:** Laporte (Suspended), Unai Egiluz (Injured), Oihan Sancet (Injured), Gorka Guruzeta (Injured)\n\n**Questionable:** Alvaro Djalo (Injured)\n\n**Getafe team news: Unal a doubt**\n\nEnes Unal was forced off with an ankle injury against Lugano in midweek with versatile defender Djene now missing through suspension after being sent off last weekend.\n\n**Predicted XI (4-4-2):** David Soria; Dani Carvajal, Abqar, Valou, Johan Mojica; Kiko Femenia, Gudelj, Mario Martin, Ramon Terrats; Martin Satriano, Ivan Azon\n\n**Unavailable:** Djene (Suspended), Uche (Injured), Juanmi (Injured)\n\n**Questionable:** Romero (Fitness), Mangala (Fitness), Unal (Injured)\n\n**Key stats**\n\n*   Eighteen of the 42 La Liga meetings since 1997/98 have been draws (43%): Athletic W13 D18 Getafe W11. \n*   Athletic are winless in the last five home meetings (D4 L1). Their last home win against Getafe was 5-1 in January 2021, the highest-scoring game in the fixture. \n*   Getafe won both meetings last season without conceding, including 1-0 at San Mamés exactly a year ago (25 October 2025). Athletic have failed to score in the last two meetings. \n*   Athletic have played only seven games – two fewer than 17 of the other 19 sides – and have nine points. They are unbeaten in five (W2 D3). \n*   Athletic have drawn their last three and have kept two straight clean sheets in 0-0 draws with Alavés and Valencia. \n*   Athletic's matches have averaged 1.86 goals this season, down from 2.66 last season. \n*   Getafe have not scored an away goal this season: four away games, four defeats, 0-8 on aggregate. \n*   Getafe have lost five consecutive La Liga away games and failed to score in six, dating back to May 2026. \n*   Getafe are unbeaten in seven home games, scoring in all seven. \n*   Getafe have scored only five goals – only one of their previous 21 La Liga seasons since 1997/98 had as few or fewer after nine games. \n*   Getafe's matches have averaged 1.78 goals this season. \n\n*Statistics are La Liga only (not all competitions)*\n\n**Athletic Bilbao vs Getafe prediction**\n\nIn nine matches in La Liga, the often tedious style of Jose Bordalas has seen Getafe score just five goals as they remain the lowest scorers in Spain’s top-flight. Athletic themselves have lacked fluency in the final third despite the intentions of manager Terzic and they will nervy about a Getafe side that may become ultra-Getafe after their hammering the other day and so a low-scoring contest feels likely for this one.\n\n**Athletic Bilbao vs Getafe tip:** Under 2.5 goals\n\nUpcoming
